4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: your live game link, your plan for which key calls which command, and 3 sentences about the Command pattern (85 points even if your game breaks), plus your live game with your three commands working (15 points).
4th Period.workingNow: Open the Google Classroom assignment called Command Pattern. Read the instructions, follow them, then fill out the exit ticket when you are done.
4th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, my turned-in game link works, and I have finished my commands or tried one Future Engineer option.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.17 — Systematically test and refine programs using a range of test cases.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through oral collaborative discussions on a range of social and academic topics.
agenda: Check your turned-in link works (5 min)
Catch up or Future Engineer (25 min)
Gallery play: try 2 classmates' games (10 min)
Exit Ticket: one command and what it does (5 min)
4th Period.connections: This week you gave every player action its own command. Today you catch up or go further, like adding on-screen buttons that call the same commands. Monday starts the Factory pattern: a BrickFactory that builds new kinds of bricks.

6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: a screenshot of your TinkerCAD lever with the fulcrum, load, and effort labeled, and its share link. A screenshot of whatever you have is 70 points, so turn it in early and update it.
6th Period.workingNow: Open the Google Classroom assignment called TinkerCAD Lever. Read the instructions, follow them, then fill out the exit ticket when you are done.
6th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, my labeled lever is turned in, and I have caught up or tried one Future Engineer option.
6th Period.contentStandard: NGSS MS-ETS1-4 — Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool, or process.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through oral collaborative discussions on a range of social and academic topics.
agenda: Check your screenshot is turned in (5 min)
Catch up or Future Engineer (25 min)
Gallery walk: see 2 classmates' levers (10 min)
Exit Ticket: where is your fulcrum? (5 min)
6th Period.connections: This week you used Align to build and label a lever in 3D. Today you catch up or go further. Monday you use the same tools to start a Warren truss bridge.

7th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Due Sunday night: your Bridge Collapse slides with the Engineer Challenge (slides 1 to 3 plus A to D: force diagram, wind test data, claim-evidence-reasoning, and your redesign). Whatever you have is 70 points, so turn it in early and update it.
7th Period.workingNow: Open the Google Classroom assignment called Bridge Collapse Slides. Read the instructions, follow them, and turn in your slides when you are done. There is no exit ticket today.
7th Period.smartGoal: By the end of class, I can defend why the bridge fell using our test data, and my slides with my own redesign are turned in.
7th Period.contentStandard: NGSS MS-ETS1-2 — Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.
7th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.9 — Expressing information and ideas in formal oral presentations on academic topics.
agenda: Engineer's briefing: 1 minute per group (12 min)
Critique: was it a fair test? (5 min)
Final check and turn in (7 min)
7th Period.connections: Yesterday you tested two decks and collected real data. Today you defend your claim to the class and design a better deck. Monday your group starts planning a bridge that won't fall, using triangles: the Warren truss.
